headline: Revenue growth accelerates, core profit growth stays thin
summary_short: PepsiCo's Q3 2026 net revenue rose 5.6% y/y to $25,274M on 3.1% organic growth; diluted EPS rose 17% to $2.23 while core EPS rose only 2% to $2.34. Full-year guidance was updated.
summary_long: Net revenue grew 5.6% on 3.1% organic growth, a 1.7-point acquisition benefit and 0.7 points from currency. International segments delivered organic volume growth; North America convenient foods improved sequentially but net pricing was lower. Operating profit rose 19% on favorable acquisition-related items and commodity mark-to-market gains; core operating profit rose 3% and core margin slipped 35bp, helped by a 4-point tariff-refund benefit. The company now guides FY2026 organic revenue of about +3%, net revenue about +6%, and core EPS +2.5% to +3.5%. Cash rose to $10,675M.

drivers.explanation: CEO Laguarta cited strength in international businesses and said structural cost reductions will be identified to fund North America investment and offset rising input cost inflation.
Growth came from 3.1% organic revenue (net pricing plus organic volume), a 1.7-point net benefit from acquisitions and divestitures, and a 0.7-point foreign exchange benefit.
Reflects a favorable net impact of acquisition and divestiture-related charges and credits, plus net mark-to-market gains on commodity derivatives; core operating profit gained less, at 3%.
EPS growth was primarily driven by operating profit growth.
Net income growth tracked operating profit growth against a higher tax provision and a swing to pension and retiree medical expense.
Revenue rose 5.6% against cost of sales up 3.7%, which lifted gross profit.

confidence_notes: Source: EX-99.1 of the 8-K filed 2026-10-08 (resolved from the 8-K cover). Quarter is the 12 weeks ended 2026-09-05. KPI values match SEC-verbatim shard data. Core (non-GAAP) EPS of $2.34 is management's measure and is not comparable to the GAAP EPS in the KPI table. The release says tariff refunds added 4 points to core operating profit growth.
